content.comment_body: Hello, Is it possible to replace a logic block, such as switching an OR gate to an AND gate, without having to redo existing wire connections? For instance, if multiple connections depart from an OR gate, can it be changed to an AND gate while retaining those links? Alternatively, can an extra block, like an AND gate, be inserted between an input and already wired outputs without deleting and reconnecting everything? I've looked for solutions but haven't found anything. Thanks.
There are two ways to do this. Please refer to the attached screen recordings.
Thank you—the first video showed exactly what I needed, it’s simple when you know how. Much appreciated!

Keep in mind: The first method only works if the new and old blocks have the same number of inputs and outputs. In that case, the old block changes color to green. If the input and output configurations differ, the old block turns red.
Also, if the blocks aren’t compatible for swapping, the original block retains a black color and doesn’t change.

analysis.insight_summary: The thread discusses how users want to modify logic diagrams (such as replacing gates or adding new blocks) without losing existing wiring. It’s possible to do this only if new and old blocks have identical input/output configurations. The software uses color indicators to show whether replacement is feasible, otherwise manual re-connection is necessary.
analysis.user_expectations: User expects to be able to replace or insert logic blocks in diagrams without needing to redo current connections, hoping for a more efficient workflow.
